name: Varadaraja Perumal Temple, Thirumanikkoodam
deity: Vishnu as Varadaraja Perumal (Manikkooda Nayakan), with Thirumamagal Nachiyar (Sridevi) and Bhudevi — Thirumanikkoodam, one of the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams
period: A Divya Desam of Chola Nadu, one of the eleven Thirunangur shrines, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
summary: At Thirunangur near Sirkazhi, Vishnu stands facing east as Varadaraja Perumal, the Manikkooda Nayakan of Thirumanikkoodam — a Divya Desam of Chola Nadu sung by Thirumangai Alvar, beside the Chandra Pushkarini.

sections.history: Thirumanikkoodam is one of the 108 Divya Desams and lies in Chola Nadu, the Kaveri delta country. It is one of the eleven Vishnu shrines of Thirunangur, a cluster of villages east of Sirkazhi, each sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Here the Lord is Varadaraja Perumal, also called Manikkooda Nayakan, standing in the nindra thirukkolam and facing east, with Thirumamagal Nachiyar and Bhudevi at his side. The name joins mani, a gem, with koodam, a peak or hall. The firm witness to the shrine is the Alvar's hymn, placed in the eighth century.
sections.architecture: The sanctum is crowned by the Kanaka vimana, and within it Varadaraja stands facing east in the standing posture. The tank belonging to the shrine is the Chandra Pushkarini, named for the Moon. It is a village temple of the Dravidian tradition, modest in scale. Thirumamagal Nachiyar and Bhudevi are worshipped beside the Lord, so that darshan here is of Varadaraja together with both his consorts.
sections.legends: Tradition holds that Chandra, the Moon, was blessed here by the Lord, which is why the tank is called the Chandra Pushkarini. A related telling belongs to all of Thirunangur: when Shiva danced at nearby Nangur, Surya and Chandra, frightened, are said to have hidden in two tanks of their own making — the Surya Pushkarini at Thiruthetriyambalam and the Chandra Pushkarini here. The wider sthala purana says that Vishnu took eleven forms at Shiva's request, and each is worshipped in its own Thirunangur shrine.
sections.festivals: Varadaraja Perumal takes part in the Thirunangur Garuda Sevai, held in the Tamil month of Thai on the day after Thai Amavasai, when the utsavars of the eleven shrines are carried on Garuda vahanams to Thirumanimadam. The Thirumangai Alvar mangalasasana utsavam, also in Thai, is the principal celebration. Confirm dates locally each year.
sections.experience: A small village shrine among the paddy fields, best visited as one stop in the round of the eleven Thirunangur Divya Desams. Look for the standing, east-facing Varadaraja and the consorts beside him, and ask after the Chandra Pushkarini. Visiting several of the eleven on one day, or timing the trip for the Thai Garuda Sevai, rewards the pilgrim most.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; the Thai Garuda Sevai is the busiest day. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirunangur lies about 8 km east of Sirkazhi, on the road towards Thiruvenkadu in Mayiladuthurai district. Sirkazhi has a railway station on the Chennai–Chidambaram–Mayiladuthurai line; the major airports are Tiruchirappalli and Chennai. Hire a vehicle or autorickshaw in Sirkazhi, since the eleven shrines lie close together.
